name: Jacob
desc: Son of Isaac; renamed Israel; father of the twelve tribes
wikipedia_summary: Jacob, later given the name Israel, is a Hebrew patriarch of the Abrahamic religions. He first appears in the Torah, where he is described in the Book of Genesis as a son of Isaac and Rebecca. Accordingly, alongside his older fraternal twin brother Esau, Jacob's paternal grandparents are Abraham and Sarah and his maternal grandfather is Bethuel, whose wife is not mentioned. He is said to have bought Esau's birthright and, with his mother's help, deceived his aging father to bless him instead of Esau. Then, following a severe drought in his homeland Canaan, Jacob and his descendants migrated to
christ_connection: Jacob, the son of Isaac and father of the twelve tribes, is typified in the New Testament as the precursor to Christ, whose journey and faith mirror Jacob's in the Book of Genesis. His wrestling with God in Gilead (Genesis 32:22-32) is a profound typology of Christ's struggle with God the Father, symbolizing the incarnation and the revelation of God's will. The covenant established between God and Jacob in Genesis 28:10-15 is fulfilled in the New Covenant through Christ, who is the promise of salvation. Jacob's faith and obedience, though imperfect, prefigure the spiritual maturity and faithfulness required of Christians, making him a key figure in the prophetic arc of sacred history leading to the Messiah.

name: David
desc: Shepherd-king of Israel; ancestor of Jesus Christ
wikipedia_summary: David was, originally, leader of the Tribe of Judah who became the first king of the united Kingdom of Israel according to the Hebrew Bible and Old Testament.

name: Moses
desc: Deliverer of Israel; received the law on Sinai
wikipedia_summary: In Abrahamic religions, Moses was the Hebrew prophet who led the Israelites out of slavery in the Exodus from Egypt. He is considered the most important prophet in Judaism and Samaritanism, and one of the most important prophets in Christianity, Islam, the Baháʼí Faith, and other Abrahamic religions. According to the Abrahamic scriptures, God dictated the Mosaic Law to Moses, which he wrote down and which formed part of the Torah.

name: Judah
desc: Son of Jacob; tribe of David and of Christ's lineage
christ_connection: Judah, as the son of Jacob and the tribe of David, is typified in the New Testament as the ancestor of Jesus Christ, fulfilling the covenantal promises made to Israel. His lineage is explicitly traced in the Book of Chronicles [Chronicles 2:12], where he is designated as the father of King David and thus the progenitor of the Messiah. The prophecy of the "Branch" in Jeremiah [Jeremiah 33:15] and the fulfillment of the "Son of David" in Psalm [Psalm 110:1] both point to Judah as the forefather of Christ, establishing a covenantal relationship that is renewed and perfected in the Messiah. The sacrificial offering of Judah in the Book of Chronicles [Chronicles 22:12] symbolizes the atonement and the redemptive work of Christ, underscoring his role as the mediator of the new covenant.

name: Jacob
desc: Son of Lehi; taught pure doctrine of Christ; author of the book of Jacob

He first appears in the Torah, where he is described in the Book of Genesis as a son of Isaac and Rebecca. Accordingly, alongside his older fraternal twin brother Esau, Jacob's paternal grandparents are Abraham and Sarah and his maternal grandfather is Bethuel, whose wife is not mentioned. He is said to have bought Esau's birthright and, with his mother's help, deceived his aging father to bless him instead of Esau. name: Nephi
desc: Son of Lehi; visionary prophet; founded the Nephite nation

name: Nephi
desc: Son of Helaman; prophet given sealing power; prayed for famine

name: Joseph
desc: Son of Jacob; sold into Egypt; type of Christ
wikipedia_summary: Joseph was a dream interpreter and considered an important Hebrew figure in the Bible's Book of Genesis.
christ_connection: Joseph, son of Jacob, is a figure who typifies the Messiah through his journey of faith and obedience, reflecting the covenantal relationship between God and His people. His experience of being sold into Egypt, where he became a servant, parallels the incarnation of Christ, who was also sold into Egypt as a servant of the Father. The covenantal promises made to Abraham and Jacob are fulfilled in Christ, who is the heir of the promise [Hebrews 12:23]. Joseph's life, marked by trials and faith, serves as a type of the suffering servant who would ultimately redeem humanity [Isaiah 53:12]. His role in the lineage of Jesus, as the father of Mary and Joseph, underscores the fulfillment of the prophecy of the Messiah in the lineage of David [Matthew 1:1-17]. The narrative of Joseph, with its themes of trust, suffering, and redemption, is a profound illustration of the redemptive work of Christ, who is both the fulfillment of the Old Testament and the beginning of the New Testament.

name: Joseph
desc: Youngest son of Lehi; given promises by his father
wikipedia_summary: Joseph is a common male name, derived from the Hebrew Yosef. "Joseph" is used, along with "Josef", mostly in English, French and partially German languages. This spelling is also found as a variant in the languages of the modern-day Nordic countries. In Portuguese and Spanish, the name is "José". In Arabic, including in the Quran, the name is spelled يوسف, Yūsuf. In Kurdish (Kurdî), the name is Ûsiv or Yûsiv, Persian, the name is Yousef, and in Turkish it is Yusuf. In Pashto the name is spelled Esaf (ايسپ) and in Malayalam it is spelled Ousep (ഔസേപ്പ്). In Tamil, it is spelled as Yosepu (யோசேப
christ_connection: [Genesis 2:24] Joseph, the youngest son of Lehi, is a figure who embodies the covenantal promise of redemption and the fulfillment of divine purpose. His lineage, though severed from the covenantal lineage of Israel, is typified in the covenant of grace, where the seed of the woman (Jesus) shall crush the head of the serpent (Satan). Joseph's role in the Book of Mormon reflects the broader narrative of salvation, where the covenantal promises are rekindled through the descendant of Lehi, who is ultimately the Christ of promise. The covenantal relationship between Joseph and his father, though severed, underscores the enduring nature of the covenant, which is fulfilled in the Christ who is the true seed of the woman.

name: Joseph Smith
desc: Prophet of the Restoration; First Vision; received and translated the Book of Mormon
wikipedia_summary: Joseph Smith Jr. was an American religious and political leader and the founder of Mormonism and the Latter Day Saint movement. Publishing the Book of Mormon at the age of 24, Smith attracted tens of thousands of followers by the time of his death fourteen years later. The religious movement he founded is followed by millions of global adherents and several churches, the largest of which is the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
christ_connection: Joseph Smith, as the prophet of the Restoration, points to Jesus Christ through the covenantal relationship established in the Book of Mormon, where the principles of the gospel are revealed in accordance with the original covenants of God. His first vision, which occurred in the autumn of 1823, typifies the fulfillment of the prophecies concerning the coming of a messenger who would bring forth the Book of Mormon and restore the true gospel of Jesus Christ. The Book of Mormon, which Joseph Smith translated, is a fulfillment of the covenantal promises made to Abraham and his descendants, thereby connecting the restoration to the eternal covenant of grace and the divine plan of salvation.

name: Aaron
desc: Brother of Moses; first high priest of Israel
wikipedia_summary: According to the Old Testament of the Bible, Aaron was an Israelite prophet, high priest, and the elder brother of Moses. Information about Aaron comes exclusively from religious texts, such as the Hebrew Bible, the New Testament, and the Quran.
christ_connection: [Aaron, the first high priest of Israel, is typified in Jesus Christ as the precursor who, through his priesthood, mediates between God and humanity. As the covenant mediator, Aaron's role in the Aaronic covenant, [Exodus 28:1-16], mirrors Jesus' role as the ultimate mediator of the new covenant, [Hebrews 7:24-25]. The sacrificial system instituted by Aaron, [Exodus 29:38-43], anticipates the ultimate sacrifice of Christ, who alone satisfies the demands of the law, [Hebrews 10:1-10]. Thus, Aaron's ministry serves as a type of Christ's priesthood, illustrating the progression from the old to the new covenant, and the fulfillment of the promise that through the Son, salvation is made possible.]

name: Aaron
desc: Son of Mosiah; missionary to Lamanites; taught the king of the Lamanites
wikipedia_summary: According to the Old Testament of the Bible, Aaron was an Israelite prophet, high priest, and the elder brother of Moses. Information about Aaron comes exclusively from religious texts, such as the Hebrew Bible, the New Testament, and the Quran.
christ_connection: [Aaron, son of Mosiah, missionary to the Lamanites, and teacher of the king of the Lamanites, is typified by the role of a prophet and teacher in the Book of Mormon, mirroring the ministry of Jesus Christ who is both the prophet and teacher of the kingdom of God. Aaron's mission to the Lamanites parallels Jesus' mission to the world, as both are called by God to proclaim the gospel and to lead the people toward salvation. The covenantal relationship established between Aaron and the Lamanites reflects the covenantal relationship between Jesus Christ and His followers, wherein Christ is the mediator and the promise-keeper of salvation.]

name: Abraham
desc: Father of the faithful; made the Abrahamic covenant
wikipedia_summary: Abraham is a patriarch revered in the Abrahamic religions, including Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. In Judaism, he is the founding father and first Hebrew patriarch who began the covenantal relationship between the Jewish people and God; in Christianity, he is the spiritual progenitor of all believers, whether Jewish or non-Jewish; and in Islam, he is a link in the chain of Islamic prophets that begins with Adam and culminates in Muhammad. Abraham is also revered in other Abrahamic religions, including the Baháʼí Faith and the Druze faith. He is regarded as the common forefather of both the
christ_connection: Abraham, as the father of the faithful, typifies the covenantal relationship between God and His people, which is fulfilled in Jesus Christ. The Abrahamic covenant, established in [Genesis 12:1-3], serves as a type of the eternal covenant that Jesus inaugurates through His death and resurrection. Through Abraham's faith and obedience, the Old Testament witnesses to the coming of the Messiah, who would bring salvation and the promise of a seed to inherit the earth. This covenantal relationship, rooted in Abraham's trust in God, is both a prefiguration and a foundation for the New Testament revelation of Jesus as the fulfillment of God's promises.

name: Saul
desc: First king of Israel
christ_connection: Saul, the first king of Israel, is typified in the covenantal relationship between God and His people, as he initially sought to destroy the worship of the Lord but later became a vessel of God's grace through the Holy Spirit. His journey from a jealous and rebellious king to a devoted follower of Christ mirrors the transformation of the Israelite nation under God's grace, as seen in the parable of the sower [Matthew 13:1-9]. The narrative of Saul's conversion and his role in the preaching of the Gospel, as recorded in the Acts of the Apostles [Acts 9:1-10], reflects the prophetic role of a king who, though initially unfaithful, is ultimately used by God to spread the Good News of salvation. The covenantal relationship established with Saul, as depicted in the Book of Samuel [1 Samuel 13:1-14], underscores the divine purpose of the Messiah, who, though not a descendant of the line of Judah, is nonetheless the fulfillment of the promises made to Israel.

name: Solomon
desc: Son of David; built the first temple; renowned for wisdom
wikipedia_summary: Solomon, also called Jedidiah, was a king of the Kingdom of Israel and Judah, according to the Hebrew Bible. The successor of his father David, he is described as the penultimate ruler of all Twelve Tribes of Israel under a united Israel and Judah. His reign is hypothesized to have lasted from c. 970–931 BCE. According to the biblical narrative, his reign brought commercial prosperity through alliances and trade, but his accumulation of wealth, horses, and foreign wives, many of whom introduced idolatry, led to divine punishment. After Solomon's death, his son Rehoboam’s harsh policies led the
christ_connection: Solomon, as the wise son of David, is typified in the Gospel of John [John 1:48] where he is described as "the Lamb of God," illustrating the divine wisdom and sacrificial nature of Christ. His construction of the first temple [1 Kings 6:1] mirrors the spiritual edifice of Christ, whose temple is the body of Christ [Ephesians 2:1-10]. Solomon's pursuit of wisdom, as recorded in [Proverbs 2:6], aligns with the spiritual quest for divine knowledge that Christ embodies, making him a precursor to the Messiah whose wisdom is both divine and redemptive.

name: Alma
desc: Priest of Noah who believed Abinadi; founded the church at the waters of Mormon
wikipedia_summary: Alma is a Nephite prophet in the Book of Mormon. Initially a priest who serves in the court of King Noah, when a prophet named Abinadi preaches to the court Alma concurs with Abinadi and affirms that what the prophet said is true. For this, Noah banishes Alma and tries to have him killed. After leaving the court, Alma goes on to found a church among Noah's subjects. He eventually leads these churchgoers out from Noah's lands, through a sojourn under Lamanite rule, and to the land of Zarahemla, where their ancestors had come from a few generations earlier, where Alma becomes high priest of the
christ_connection: Alma, as a priest of Noah, was part of the covenantal lineage established by Abraham and Isaac, and his role as a founder of the church at the waters of Mormon reflects the establishment of a new covenant in the latter days. His belief in Abinadi, a prophet who spoke of the coming of a Messiah, points to the fulfillment of the prophecies concerning the Lord Jesus Christ, who is the Messiah foretold in the Book of Mormon. Alma's actions and teachings align with the doctrine of the Lord Jesus Christ, as he sought to establish a church in accordance with the covenantal promises made through the prophets, thereby connecting his ministry to the broader narrative of salvation and the restoration of the gospel.

name: Alma the Younger
desc: Son of Alma; angel-rebuked sinner turned mighty prophet and judge
wikipedia_summary: In the Book of Mormon, Alma, the son of Alma is a Nephite prophet often referred to as Alma the Younger to distinguish him from his father, who is often referred to as Alma the Elder. These appellations, "the Younger" and "the Elder," are not used in the Book of Mormon; they are distinctions made by scholars, useful because both individuals were prominent during the same portion of the Book of Mormon's narrative and filled a similar cultural and religious role. Alma is the namesake of the Book of Alma.
christ_connection: Alma the Younger, as a figure in the Book of Mormon, serves as a typological precursor to Jesus Christ, embodying the virtues and trials of the Messiah. His sinfulness and subsequent repentance mirror the moral and spiritual journey of Christ, illustrating the covenantal relationship between God and His people. The divine retribution against Alma, as recounted in [1 Nephi 13:23], parallels the ultimate judgment and redemption of Jesus, underscoring the fulfillment of prophecies concerning the coming of the Messiah. Alma's role as a prophet and judge also reflects the broader role of Christ as the ultimate interpreter of divine will and the preserver of the covenant.

name: Ammon
desc: Son of Mosiah; missionary to the Lamanites; defender of the king's flocks
wikipedia_summary: Ammon was an ancient Semitic-speaking kingdom occupying the east of the Jordan River, between the torrent valleys of Arnon and Jabbok, in present-day Jordan. The chief city of the country was Rabbah or Rabbat Ammon, site of the modern city of Amman, Jordan's capital. Milcom and Molech are named in the Hebrew Bible as the gods of Ammon. The people of this kingdom are called Children of Ammon or Ammonites.
christ_connection: [1 Corinthians 1:10] Ammon, as a prophet and missionary, exemplifies the spirit of the gospel through his dedication to the Lamanites, reflecting the universal call of Christ to all peoples. His role in defending the king's flocks parallels the restoration of the gospel through the priesthood and the preservation of sacred truths, which are essential for the salvation of the world. As a figure in the Book of Mormon, Ammon's mission and teachings serve as a type of the gospel preached by Jesus Christ, emphasizing the importance of missionary work and the defense of sacred doctrines in the latter days.

name: Peter
desc: Chief Apostle; received keys of the kingdom; also called Simon, Cephas

name: Joshua
desc: Successor of Moses; led Israel into Canaan
wikipedia_summary: Joshua, also known as Yehoshua, Jehoshua, or Josue, was Moses' assistant in the books of Exodus and Numbers, and later succeeded Moses as leader of the Israelite tribes in the Book of Joshua of the Hebrew Bible. His name was Hoshea the son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, but Moses called him "Yehoshua", the name by which he is commonly known in English. According to the Bible, he was born in Egypt prior to the Exodus.

name: Captain Moroni
desc: Commander of the Nephite armies; raised the Title of Liberty
wikipedia_summary: According to the Book of Mormon, Captain Moroni was an important Nephite military commander who lived during the first century BC. He is first mentioned in the Book of Alma as "the chief captain over the Nephites."

name: Moroni
desc: Son of Mormon; sealed the plates; visited Joseph Smith as an angel
wikipedia_summary: Moroni is described in the Book of Mormon as the last Nephite prophet, historian, and military commander who, according to the faith of the Latter Day Saint movement, became the Angel Moroni who presented the golden plates to Joseph Smith.

name: Angel Moroni
desc: Resurrected Moroni who delivered the gold plates to Joseph Smith; appeared September 1823
wikipedia_summary: The angel Moroni is an angel whom Joseph Smith, founder of the Latter Day Saint movement, reported as having visited him on numerous occasions, beginning on September 21, 1823. According to Smith, the angel Moroni was the guardian of the golden plates buried near his home in western New York, which Latter Day Saints believe were the source of the Book of Mormon. An important figure in the theology of the Latter Day Saint movement, Moroni is featured prominently in its architecture and art. Besides Smith, the Three Witnesses and several other witnesses also reported that they saw Moroni in visi
christ_connection: Angel Moroni, as a resurrected figure in the Restoration movement, serves as a typological precursor to Jesus Christ, embodying the spirit of the covenant established between God and His people. His resurrection and commissioning to deliver the gold plates align with the divine purpose of the Messiah, who was also raised from the dead and entrusted with the sacred mission of revealing God's will. The prophetic role of Moroni reflects the broader narrative of salvation history, wherein the resurrected Christ is the ultimate mediator and deliverer of divine truth. [Book Chapter:2 Nephi 25:21]

name: John the Baptist
desc: Forerunner of Christ; baptized Jesus in the Jordan River
wikipedia_summary: John the Baptist was a Jewish preacher active in the area of the Jordan River in the early first century AD. He is also known as Saint John the Forerunner in Eastern Orthodoxy and Oriental Orthodoxy, Saint John the Immerser in the Baptist tradition, and as the prophet Yahya ibn Zakariya in Islam. He is sometimes referred to as John the Baptiser.
christ_connection: John the Baptist, as the forerunner of Christ, points to Jesus Christ through the covenantal relationship established in the Old Testament, where the role of a prophet was foretold in the Book of Isaiah [Isaiah 40:3]. His ministry typifies the sacrificial nature of the Messiah, as seen in the Book of Hosea [Hosea 3:1], and his baptism of Jesus in the Jordan River [Matthew 3:16] fulfills the prophecy of the Lamb of God [John 1:29]. The covenantal promise of a precursor to the Messiah, as outlined in the Book of Deuteronomy [Deuteronomy 18:18], is fulfilled in John's role, establishing the foundation for the New Covenant through Jesus Christ.

name: Benjamin
desc: Youngest son of Jacob and Rachel; tribe of Saul and Paul
wikipedia_summary: Benjamin was the younger of the two sons of Jacob and Rachel, and Jacob's twelfth and youngest son overall in Jewish, Christian and Islamic tradition. He was also considered the progenitor of the Israelite Tribe of Benjamin. Unlike Rachel's first son, Joseph, Benjamin was born in Canaan according to biblical narrative.
christ_connection: Benjamin, as the youngest son of Jacob and Rachel, is typified in the Gospel of Matthew [Matthew 1:1-17], where he is introduced as the son of Joseph, the earthly father of Jesus. This typological connection reflects the covenantal relationship between God and Israel, with Benjamin symbolizing the future Messiah whose lineage is ultimately traced through Joseph, the earthly father of Jesus. The narrative of Benjamin's birth and early life parallels the prophetic fulfillment of the promise made to Jacob, underscoring the continuity between the Old and New Testaments and the fulfillment of the covenantal promises through Jesus Christ.

name: King Benjamin
desc: Righteous Nephite king whose address proclaimed Christ's atoning name

name: Samuel
desc: Prophet, judge, and kingmaker of Israel
christ_connection: Samuel, as the prophet and judge of Israel, serves as a typological figure in the Old Testament, prefiguring the Messiah through his role in anointing a king and establishing the covenant. His commission in [1 Samuel 3:1-10] is fulfilled in Jesus Christ, who is both the anointed king and the fulfillment of the covenant promises. The narrative of Samuel's calling and his interactions with the people mirror the spiritual journey of Jesus, who is the ultimate revelation of God's will and the mediator between God and humanity. The covenantal relationship established by Samuel typifies the eternal covenant between God and His people, which is fully realized in Christ.

name: Ephraim
desc: Son of Joseph; the 'stick of Ephraim' in Ezekiel 37; central to Book of Mormon lineage
wikipedia_summary: Ephraim was, according to the Book of Genesis, the second son of Joseph ben Jacob and Asenath, as well as the adopted son of his biological grandfather Jacob, making him the progenitor of the Tribe of Ephraim.

name: Samuel the Lamanite
desc: Lamanite prophet who prophesied from the walls of Zarahemla
wikipedia_summary: According to the Book of Mormon, Samuel the Lamanite is a prophet who lived in the ancient Americas, sent by Jesus Christ around 5 BC to teach and warn the Nephites just before his birth in the Old World. The account is recorded in Helaman 13–16.

name: Paul
desc: Apostle to the Gentiles; formerly Saul of Tarsus

name: Isaac
desc: Son of Abraham and Sarah; carried the covenant
wikipedia_summary: Isaac is one of the three patriarchs of the Israelites and an important figure in the Abrahamic religions, including Judaism, Samaritanism, Christianity, Islam, the Baháʼí Faith, and Rastafari. Isaac first appears in the Torah, in which he is the son of Abraham and Sarah, the father of Jacob and Esau, and the grandfather of the twelve tribes of Israel.
christ_connection: Isaac, as the son of Abraham and Sarah, embodies the covenantal promise of God, who through him would bless all nations (Genesis 22:18). His role as the heir of the covenant reflects the fulfillment of the promise that one descendant of Abraham would be the heir of the covenant, thereby pointing to the Messiah. The covenantal relationship established between God and Abraham, which is typified in Isaac, underscores the divine purpose of Jesus as the ultimate heir of the covenant, through whom God's promises are fulfilled. The covenantal nature of Isaac's lineage illustrates the continuity of the divine promise, with Jesus as the final and complete fulfillment of the covenantal oath.

name: Jeremiah
desc: Weeping prophet of Judah; foretold the Babylonian captivity
wikipedia_summary: Jeremiah, also called Jeremias, and occasionally in older English texts Jeremy, was one of the major prophets of the Hebrew Bible. According to Jewish tradition, Jeremiah authored the book that bears his name, the Books of Kings, and the Book of Lamentations, with the assistance and under the editorship of Baruch ben Neriah, his scribe and disciple.

name: Manasseh
desc: Son of Joseph; tribe divided east and west of Jordan
wikipedia_summary: Manasseh is both a given name and a surname. Its variants include Manasses and Manasse.

name: Manasseh
desc: Wicked king of Judah who repented in Babylonian captivity
wikipedia_summary: Manasseh is both a given name and a surname. Its variants include Manasses and Manasse.
christ_connection: Manasseh, the wicked king of Judah who repented in Babylonian captivity, points to Jesus Christ through the lens of covenant and typology. His repentance, though marked by a temporary cessation of idolatry, reflects the broader theological theme of divine mercy and the eventual restoration of the covenant people. The narrative of Manasseh, recorded in [2 Kings 23:1-2], serves as a type of Christ's own repentance and eventual return to God, illustrating the cyclical nature of salvation history. The covenantal relationship established with Manasseh, though broken, underscores the enduring nature of God's promises and the ultimate fulfillment of the covenant in the person of Jesus Christ.

name: Adam
desc: First man; father of the human family
wikipedia_summary: Adam is the name given in Genesis 1–5 to the first human. Adam is the first human being aware of God, and features as such in various belief systems.
christ_connection: Adam, as the first man and father of the human family, serves as a typological precursor to Jesus Christ. His creation and fall exemplify the covenantal relationship between God and humanity, foreshadowing the redemptive work of Christ who fulfills the promise of salvation. The narrative of Adam's sin and subsequent judgment mirrors the sacrificial nature of Christ's atonement, wherein both figure out of the divine plan of redemption. [Genesis 3:15][Genesis 5:24]

name: Noah
desc: Builder of the ark; survived the flood
wikipedia_summary: Noah appears as the last of the Antediluvian patriarchs in the traditions of Abrahamic religions. His story appears in the Hebrew Bible, the Quran and Baha'i writings, and extracanonically.

name: King Noah
desc: Wicked Nephite king who burned Abinadi
wikipedia_summary: King Noah is a Nephite king in the Book of Mormon who appears in the Book of Mosiah. Noah rules over a colony of Nephites who come from Zarahemla and settle in the land of Lehi-Nephi, succeeding his father, Zeniff. In the Book of Mosiah, King Noah distances from his father's teachings, committing what the text calls "all manner of wickedness." Noah and his priests sentence a prophet named Abinadi, who prophesies of his kingdom's downfall if they did not repent, to death by fire. During a Lamanite invasion, Noah and some of his people flee the land, and those who remain are subjected to Lamanit
christ_connection: [Genesis 6:1-2] King Noah, a wicked Nephite king, is depicted as one who burned Abinadi, a prophet of God, and whose actions reflect the consequences of rejecting divine revelation. This figure typifies the broader moral and spiritual decay that precedes the coming of Christ, illustrating the covenantal responsibility of rulers to uphold righteousness. The narrative of King Noah serves as a cautionary tale, pointing to the necessity of divine intervention and the restoration of covenantal purity, which ultimately finds its fulfillment in the redemptive work of Jesus Christ.

name: Joab
desc: Commander of David's army; loyal but ruthless; killed by Solomon's command
wikipedia_summary: Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was the nephew of King David and the commander of his army according to the Hebrew Bible.

name: Lot
desc: Nephew of Abraham; rescued from Sodom; type of partial obedience

name: Hezekiah
desc: Righteous king of Judah; destroyed the Nehushtan; life extended fifteen years in answer to prayer
wikipedia_summary: Hezekiah, or Ezekias, was the son of Ahaz and the thirteenth king of Judah according to the Hebrew Bible. He is described as "the best-attested figure in biblical history," due to the extensive documentation of his reign in biblical texts and external sources. His reign was marked by his significant religious reforms and his revolt against the Assyrian Empire. He witnessed the destruction of the northern Kingdom of Israel by the Assyrians under Sargon II in c. 722 BC and later faced the Assyrian siege of Jerusalem by King Sennacherib in 701 BC.

name: Lehi
desc: Prophet-patriarch who led his family from Jerusalem to the promised land

name: Elijah
desc: Prophet who confronted Baal worship; translated; returned as Elias
wikipedia_summary: Elijah was a prophet and miracle worker who lived in the northern kingdom of Israel during the reign of King Ahab, according to the Books of Kings in the Hebrew Bible.

name: Isaiah
desc: Prophet whose writings are quoted most in the Book of Mormon
wikipedia_summary: Isaiah was the 8th-century BC Israelite prophet after whom the Book of Isaiah is named.

name: Jeroboam
desc: First king of northern Israel after the split; set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan
wikipedia_summary: Jeroboam I, frequently cited Jeroboam son of Nebat, was, according to the Hebrew Bible, the first king of the northern Kingdom of Israel following a revolt of the ten tribes against Rehoboam that put an end to the United Monarchy. According to the book of 1 Kings, he reigned for 22 years and "there was war continually between Rehoboam and Jeroboam". Jeroboam also fought Abijam son of Rehoboam king of Judah. Jeroboam is often described as "doing evil in the sight of the Lord"
christ_connection: [Jeroboam] serves as a typological figure in the Old Testament, illustrating the principle of divine covenant and the consequences of idolatry. His establishment of golden calves at Bethel and Dan, as recorded in [1 Kings 12:25], mirrors the later institution of the Eucharist in Christianity, where the bread and wine symbolize the body and blood of Christ. This act of idolatry, which led to spiritual decline and national ruin, parallels the spiritual and moral consequences faced by the Christian community when it forsakes the Lord. Thus, Jeroboam's story functions as a prophetic warning, emphasizing the importance of fidelity to God and the dangers of idolatry, which ultimately connect to the broader narrative of salvation through Jesus Christ.

name: Matthew
desc: Apostle; former publican; author of first Gospel
christ_connection: Matthew, as the Apostle and author of the first Gospel, serves as a foundational figure in the narrative of salvation history. His ministry as a publican, marked by humility and repentance, typifies the spiritual transformation required for discipleship, reflecting the covenantal promise of grace and the call to follow Christ. The Gospel of Matthew, with its emphasis on the Law, the Kingdom of Heaven, and the Beatitudes, structures the theological framework that prepares the audience for the coming of Jesus, thus connecting the Old and New Testaments through the lens of covenant and prophecy. The detailed structure of Matthew’s Gospel, with its parables, teachings, and symbolic imagery, not only records the life of Christ but also establishes the doctrinal foundations that culminate in the revelation of His nature and mission.

name: Absalom
desc: Son of David; rebelled against his father; died caught in a tree
wikipedia_summary: Absalom, according to the Hebrew Bible, was an Israelite prince. Born to David and Maacah, who was from Geshur, he was the only full sibling of Tamar. He is described in the Hebrew Bible as being exceptionally beautiful, as is his sister. In the narrative of 2 Samuel 13, his sister Tamar takes refuge at his house after she is raped by their paternal half-brother Amnon ; David is angered by the incident, but does nothing, as Amnon is his heir apparent. Infuriated by the rape and David's inaction, Absalom assassinates Amnon and subsequently flees to Geshur, which is ruled by his and Tamar's mate
christ_connection: Absalom, son of David, typifies the sin of rebellion against divine authority and the consequence of forsaking the covenant. His death, described in [1 Samuel 31:6], mirrors the ultimate sacrifice of Jesus, who also bore the punishment for sin. As a figure in the Old Testament, Absalom serves as a precursor to Christ, illustrating the theme of divine judgment and the necessity of redemption through the Messiah. The narrative of Absalom's downfall underscores the covenantal relationship between God and His people, and his fate foreshadows the redemptive work of Jesus, who fulfills the promises made to Israel through the line of David.

name: Daniel
desc: Prophet in Babylon; interpreted dreams and visions

name: Ahab
desc: Wicked king of Israel; married Jezebel; confronted by Elijah on Carmel
wikipedia_summary: Ahab was a king of Israel, the son and successor of King Omri, and the husband of Jezebel of Sidon, according to the Hebrew Bible. He is depicted in the Bible as a Baal worshipper and is criticized for causing moral decline in Israel, though modern scholars question this.

name: Job
desc: Righteous man tested with suffering; affirmed the Resurrection
christ_connection: Job, a figure in the Old Testament, is depicted as a righteous man subjected to severe trials, mirroring the suffering of Christ. His steadfast faith and perseverance, as recorded in [Job 42:7], reflect the divine nature of Jesus, who also endured suffering and ultimate sacrifice. The covenantal relationship established between God and Job, as seen in [Job 1:1-12], parallels the covenantal promises extended to Jesus through the New Covenant. Job's affirmation of the Resurrection, as expressed in [Job 19:25-26], anticipates the fulfillment of Christ's resurrection, thereby connecting Job to the ultimate redemptive work of Jesus.

name: Levi
desc: Son of Jacob; progenitor of the priestly tribe
wikipedia_summary: Levi was, according to the Book of Genesis, the third of the six sons of Jacob and Leah, and the founder of the Israelite Tribe of Levi and the great-grandfather of Aaron, Moses and Miriam. Certain religious and political functions were reserved for the Levites.

name: Mosiah
desc: Prophet-king; translator of the Jaredite record
christ_connection: Mosiah, as a prophet-king in the Book of Mormon, serves as a typological figure whose role in the covenantal narrative points directly to Jesus Christ. His commission as a translator of the Jaredite record parallels the divine mission of Christ, who is both the fulfillment of ancient prophecies and the mediator of the new covenant. The covenantal relationship established through Mosiah's leadership anticipates the eternal priesthood and redemptive work of Christ, which is central to the gospel of Jesus Christ. The Book of Mormon's emphasis on divine revelation and the restoration of the gospel mirrors the spiritual depth and divine authority that Christ embodies, making Mosiah a key figure in the prophetic lineage leading to the Messiah.

name: Jared
desc: Brother's unnamed companion; led the Jaredites to the promised land
wikipedia_summary: Jared is a given name of Biblical derivation.
christ_connection: Jared, as the unnamed companion of Abraham in the Book of Mormon, serves as a typological figure who prefigures the role of Christ in the covenant of grace. His leadership and guidance in guiding the Jaredites to the promised land mirror the divine mission of Christ, who is both the mediator of the covenant and the fulfillment of the promises made to the fathers. The narrative of Jared's journey reflects the arc of sacred history, wherein the descendants of Adam are brought forth through divine intervention, ultimately pointing to the coming of the Messiah. [Jacob 1:43; 1 Nephi 13:24]

name: Ishmael
desc: Son of Abraham and Hagar; patriarch of the Arab peoples
wikipedia_summary: In the biblical Book of Genesis, Ishmael was the first son of Abraham. His mother was Hagar, the handmaiden of Abraham's wife Sarah. He died at the age of 137.
christ_connection: Ishmael, the son of Abraham and Hagar, is a figure who points to the covenantal relationship between God and His people, particularly through the lens of the law and the promise. As the patriarch of the Arab peoples, Ishmael's story is embedded in the narrative of divine sovereignty and the fulfillment of God's covenantal promises. His existence typifies the struggle between the law and the Spirit, as he is cast out by Isaac and becomes the ancestor of the people of Arab descent, who later become the custodians of the covenantal legacy. This lineage is ultimately connected to Jesus Christ through the covenantal promise that the seed of the woman shall crush the head of the serpent (Genesis 3:15), thereby establishing a prophetic connection where Ishmael's descendants are foretold to bear the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23).

name: Jehoshaphat
desc: Righteous king of Judah; allied with Ahab; called on prophets before battle
wikipedia_summary: Jehoshaphat, according to the Hebrew Bible, was the son of Asa, and the fourth king of the Kingdom of Judah, in succession to his father. His children included Jehoram, who succeeded him as king. His mother was Azubah. Historically, his name has sometimes been connected with the Valley of Josaphat.
christ_connection: Jehoshaphat, as a righteous king of Judah, typifies the ideal ruler who walks in obedience to God, reflecting the moral and spiritual standards that Jesus Christ embodies. His alliance with Ahab, though flawed, illustrates the complex relationships within the kingdom of Israel, a precursor to the Church and the New Covenant. Jehoshaphat's call upon the prophets before his battle underscores the importance of divine guidance and the covenantal relationship between God and His people, which Jesus Christ fulfills through His sacrificial death and resurrection. This figure connects to Jesus Christ through the lens of covenantal fidelity, moral integrity, and the divine call to righteousness, all of which are central to the New Testament revelation.

name: Enoch
desc: Prophet who built Zion; translated without death
wikipedia_summary: Enoch is a biblical figure and patriarch prior to Noah's flood. He is the son of Jared and father of Methuselah.
christ_connection: Enoch, as a prophet in the Old Testament, is depicted as having walked with God and been translated without death, a phenomenon that typifies the eternal nature of the divine presence and the promise of a future resurrection. His ascension serves as a prefiguration of the heavenly calling of Jesus, who is also promised to return to heaven and reign eternally. The covenantal relationship established between Enoch and God parallels the eternal covenant between God and Jesus, emphasizing the divine promise of life beyond death and the fulfillment of the covenantal oath in the person of Christ. Enoch's role in building Zion, a sanctuary of divine habitation, further connects him to the prophetic role of Jesus, who is described as the "stone" through which the church is built and the foundation of the new covenant.

name: Reuben
desc: Firstborn of Jacob; lost birthright through transgression
wikipedia_summary: Reuben or Reuven is a Biblical male first name from Hebrew רְאוּבֵן (Re'uven), meaning "behold, a son". In the Bible, Reuben was the firstborn son of Jacob.
christ_connection: Reuben, the firstborn of Jacob, is typified by Jesus Christ in the context of the covenantal relationship between God and His people. As the figure who lost his birthright through transgression, Reuben serves as a type of Christ, who, though born of a woman, was rejected by the patriarchal hierarchy and ultimately became the mediator of the new covenant. [Genesis 35:22] [Hebrews 5:10] The loss of the birthright symbolizes the forfeiture of divine favor and the subsequent redemption through Christ, who was born of a woman and was ultimately exalted as the head of the new covenant.

name: Dan
desc: Son of Jacob by Bilhah; tribe settled in the north
christ_connection: Dan, son of Jacob by Bilhah, is typified in the Gospel of Matthew [Matthew 2:14], where he is referred to as the "father of the house of Jacob" and the "father of the house of Joseph," thereby establishing a lineage that parallels the lineage of Jesus Christ. This typological connection reflects the covenantal relationship between God and Israel, wherein Dan's role as a patriarchal figure prefigures the role of Jesus as the Messiah. The narrative of Dan's lineage, rooted in the Old Testament, serves as a foretelling of the redemptive plan of God, wherein Jesus Christ is both the fulfillment of the covenant and the culmination of the prophetic line of Israel.

name: Gad
desc: Son of Jacob; tribe settled east of the Jordan
christ_connection: Gad, son of Jacob, is typified in the covenantal relationship between God and His people, as he represents the covenantal role of a leader who is entrusted with the responsibilities of the tribe of Judah. His lineage is traced through the line of Abraham and Isaac, culminating in the Messiah, who is the fulfillment of the covenant promises made to Israel. The covenantal relationship established through Gad reflects the divine purpose of salvation, as the Lord promises to bless the tribes and establish a kingdom through His servant, Jesus Christ. This typological connection underscores the continuity of the covenant and the prophetic fulfillment of the promise that the Messiah would come to restore and bless the people of God.

name: Zedekiah
desc: Last king of Judah before the Babylonian captivity
wikipedia_summary: Zedekiah was the twentieth and final King of Judah before the destruction of Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar II of Babylon.
christ_connection: Zedekiah, the last king of Judah before the Babylonian captivity, is typified in the Gospel of Matthew, where Jesus is referred to as the "Son of David" [Matthew 1:1], thereby establishing a lineage that parallels the royal line of Judah. His reign, marked by moral decline and the eventual fall of the kingdom, foreshadows the sacrificial atonement and ultimate redemption of Jesus Christ, who fulfills the covenantal promises made to David and Judah. The narrative of Zedekiah's downfall and the subsequent exile mirrors the broader historical trajectory of Israel, culminating in the redemptive work of Christ who brings about the restoration of the covenant through His resurrection and ascension.

name: Gideon
desc: Judge who delivered Israel from Midian
wikipedia_summary: Gideon also named Jerubbaal and Jerubbesheth was an Israelite shopeṭ ("judge"), military leader, and prophet whose calling and victory over the Midianites is described in Judges 6–8 in the Hebrew Bible.
christ_connection: Gideon, the judge of Israel, is typified in Jesus Christ through the imagery of the "stone" that became "great" (1 Samuel 2:10), a metaphor that parallels the crucifixion and resurrection of Christ. As a figure of covenant faithfulness, Gideon's victory over the Midianites reflects the fulfillment of the covenantal promise made to Israel, which is ultimately fulfilled in the redemptive work of Christ. The narrative of Gideon, marked by divine intervention and the triumph of a humble leader, parallels the redemptive role of Jesus, who, though despised, is the cornerstone of the covenantal salvation. The story of Gideon thus serves as a prophetic type, illustrating the coming of Christ who would break the chains of oppression and restore the people of God.

name: Gideon
desc: Nephite soldier who opposed King Noah; killed by Nehor; honored with a city
wikipedia_summary: Gideon also named Jerubbaal and Jerubbesheth was an Israelite shopeṭ ("judge"), military leader, and prophet whose calling and victory over the Midianites is described in Judges 6–8 in the Hebrew Bible.
christ_connection: [Gideon's elevation to a city reflects the covenantal promise extended to the faithful, as seen in the Book of Mormon, where the city of Gideon is established as a testament to the divine calling and the fulfillment of the covenantal promise. The narrative of Gideon, who was chosen by God to deliver the people from the Ammonites, parallels the role of Jesus Christ as the Messiah, who was chosen by God to deliver the people of Israel from bondage and to establish a new covenant. The city of Gideon, as a type of the New Jerusalem, symbolizes the eternal kingdom of God, which is ultimately fulfilled in the person of Jesus Christ. The story of Gideon, therefore, typifies the process of divine selection and the establishment of a new covenant, which is central to the theology of Jesus Christ as the Messiah and the Savior of the world.]

name: Helaman
desc: Son of Alma; commander of the stripling warriors; prophet
wikipedia_summary: The Book of Mormon mentions three men named Helaman. The first was the son of King Benjamin, king of the united Nephite-Zarahemla kingdom who lived in the 2nd century BC. Besides his genealogy, information about the first Helaman is limited. His brother, Mosiah, became heir to the throne.
christ_connection: Helaman, as the son of Alma and commander of the stripling warriors, is typified by the role of a prophet in the Book of Mormon, reflecting the covenantal relationship between God and His people. His leadership and divine calling mirror the prophetic function of Jesus Christ, who is both the mediator of the covenant and the fulfillment of ancient prophecies. The spiritual authority and divine commission bestowed upon Helaman parallel the authority and mission of Jesus Christ, who is the ultimate prophet and redeemer of the world. [1 Nephi 1:10][2 Nephi 1:10]

name: Amulek
desc: Companion to Alma the Younger; witness of the living Christ in Ammonihah
wikipedia_summary: Amulek is a man referred to in the Book of Alma, a section of the Book of Mormon. After being visited by an angel, he gives food to the prophet Alma, listens to his preaching, and becomes his missionary companion. Alma and Amulek preach in Ammonihah and are challenged by lawyers, primarily Zeezrom, who accuses Amulek of lying and teaching against their laws. They are brought before the chief judge of the land. The men who believe their teachings are thrown out of the city and the women and children are burned in a fire, which Alma and Amulek are made to watch. Then, they are imprisoned until A
christ_connection: Amulek, as a companion to Alma the Younger and a witness of the living Christ in Ammonihah, serves as a typological precursor to the ministry of Jesus Christ. His testimony aligns with the covenantal relationship established between God and His people, reflecting the promises of the Book of Mormon and the broader biblical narrative. Amulek's role in the Book of Mormon underscores the continuity of divine revelation and the fulfillment of prophecies concerning the coming of the Messiah, thereby connecting him to the eternal covenant and the redemptive work of Jesus Christ. The scriptural context of Amulek's ministry illustrates the doctrine of the living Christ, emphasizing the divine authority and the redemptive purpose of Christ's ministry.

name: Coriantumr
desc: Last surviving Jaredite king; witnessed the destruction of his people
christ_connection: Coriantumr, the last surviving Jaredite king, is typified by Jesus Christ in the sense that both are figures of covenantal significance, entrusted with the responsibility of preserving the lineage of Noah and the covenantal promises of God. As a prophet and leader, Coriantumr's role mirrors that of Christ, who is both the fulfillment of ancient prophecies and the mediator of the new covenant. The destruction of Coriantumr's people, as recounted in [Book of Mormon 1:3], parallels the ultimate judgment and restoration that Christ brings about, fulfilling the prophecy that "the Lord shall come to his own, and the people shall be gathered" [Book of Mormon 1:4], thus connecting Coriantumr to the broader narrative of salvation and covenantal renewal.

name: Balaam
desc: Prophet-for-hire hired to curse Israel; prophesied of the Star out of Jacob
wikipedia_summary:
Balaam, son of Beor, was, according to the Bible, a gentile prophet and diviner who lived in Pethor, a place identified with the ancient city of Pitru, thought to have been located between the region of Iraq and northern Syria in what is now southeastern Turkey. According to chapters 22–24 of the Book of Numbers, he was hired by King Balak of Moab to curse Israel, but instead he blessed the Israelites, as dictated by God. Subsequently, the plan to entice the Israelites into idol worship and sexual immorality is attributed to him.
Balaam is also mentioned in the Book of Micah, the Second Epistl

name: Asa
desc: King of Judah who removed idols and trusted the Lord early in his reign
christ_connection: [2 Samuel 7:12-13] Asa, king of Judah, was a figure who removed idols and trusted the Lord early in his reign, reflecting a covenantal faith that anticipated the Messiah. His devotion to the Lord, despite the idolatrous practices of his predecessors, typifies the early stages of the covenantal relationship between God and His people, which would culminate in the coming of Jesus Christ. Asa's actions, though not fully realized in his lifetime, serve as a precursor to the prophetic fulfillment of the covenant, wherein the Lord promises to establish an everlasting kingdom through the descendant of David, thereby connecting Asa to the eternal promise of salvation through Christ.

name: Amalickiah
desc: Nephite dissenter who became king of the Lamanites through treachery; killed by Teancum
wikipedia_summary: In the Book of Mormon, Amalickiah was a Nephite dissenter. His first appearance in the text is as a political dissident with aspirations to re-establish a monarchy. Later, after seizing the Lamanite throne, Amalickiah led a war to enslave the Nephites. After his death he was succeeded by his brother Ammoron. The story appears in the latter half of the Book of Alma.

name: Sidney Rigdon
desc: Early convert and counselor to Joseph Smith; scribe for the Joseph Smith Translation
wikipedia_summary: Sidney Rigdon was a leader during the early history of the Latter Day Saint movement.
christ_connection: Sidney Rigdon, as an early convert and counselor to Joseph Smith, serves as a typological figure within the restoration movement, reflecting the spiritual and doctrinal foundations of the Latter Day Saint tradition. His role as a scribe for the Joseph Smith Translation underscores his commitment to the divine revelation of scripture, aligning him with the covenantal relationship between God and His people. Rigdon's theological engagement with scripture, particularly in the context of the Book of Mormon and the Book of Revelation, illustrates the prophetic nature of the restoration movement, which seeks to restore the original teachings of Jesus Christ. His work exemplifies the doctrine of the priesthood and the importance of scripture in the life of a Latter Day Saint, thus connecting him to the broader narrative of Christ's redemptive work through the covenantal and typological dimensions of sacred history.

name: Pilate
desc: Roman governor who sentenced Jesus to crucifixion
wikipedia_summary: Pontius Pilate was the fifth governor of the Roman province of Judaea, serving under Emperor Tiberius from 26/27 to 36/37 AD. He is best known for being the official who presided over the trial of Jesus and ultimately ordered his crucifixion. Pilate's importance in Christianity is underscored by his prominent place in both the Apostles' and Nicene Creeds. Because the gospels portray Pilate as reluctant to execute Jesus, the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church believes that Pilate became a Christian and venerates him as both a martyr and a saint, a belief which was also historically held by the

name: Sarah
desc: Wife of Abraham; mother of Isaac
wikipedia_summary: Sarah is a biblical matriarch, prophet, and major figure in Abrahamic religions. While different Abrahamic faiths portray her differently, Judaism, Christianity, and Islam all depict her character similarly, as that of a pious woman, renowned for her hospitality and beauty, the wife of Abraham, and the mother of Isaac. Sarah has her feast day on 1 September in the Catholic Church, 19 August in the Coptic Orthodox Church, 20 January in the LCMS, and 12 and 20 December in the Eastern Orthodox Church.
christ_connection: Sarah, as the wife of Abraham and mother of Isaac, is a figure deeply embedded in the covenantal narrative of the Old Testament. Her relationship with Abraham reflects the foundational covenantal bond between God and His people, a relationship that finds its fulfillment in Jesus Christ. Sarah's faith and obedience exemplify the moral and spiritual standards that God demands, which are ultimately realized in the incarnate Son. The covenantal promises made to Abraham, such as the promise of a descendant through Sarah, are typified in Jesus, who is the heir of the promise and the fulfillment of the covenantal oath. Thus, Sarah's role in the biblical narrative serves as a precursor to Christ, illustrating the continuity of divine purpose and the gradual unfolding of salvation history.

name: Zechariah
desc: Post-exile prophet; messianic visions of the Branch

name: Elisha
desc: Successor of Elijah; performed many miracles
wikipedia_summary: Elisha was, according to the Hebrew Bible, an Israelite prophet and a wonder-worker. His name is commonly transliterated into English as Elisha via Hebrew, Eliseus via Greek and Latin, Ełishe (Yeghishe/Elisha) via Armenian or Alyasa via Arabic, and Elyasa or Elyesa via Turkish. Also mentioned in the New Testament and the Quran,[6:86][38:48] Elisha is venerated as a prophet in Judaism, Christianity and Islam and writings of the Bahá'í Faith refer to him by name.

name: Mordecai
desc: Uncle of Esther; refused to bow to Haman; instrumental in saving the Jews
wikipedia_summary: Mordecai is one of the main personalities in the Book of Esther in the Hebrew Bible. He is the cousin and guardian of Esther, who became queen of Persia under the reign of Ahasuerus. The king's grand vizier Haman is offended by Mordecai because of his refusal to bow before him, and when confronted, Mordecai's excuse was simply that he was a Jew. Consequently, Haman plots to have all of Persia's Jews killed, and eventually convinces Ahasuerus to permit him to do so. Mordecai's loyalty and bravery are highlighted throughout the story as he convinces Esther to use her position as queen to foil th

name: James
desc: Apostle; son of Zebedee; brother of John
wikipedia_summary: James the Great was one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus. According to the New Testament, he was the second of the apostles to die, after Judas Iscariot, and the first to be martyred. Saint James is the patron saint of Spain and, according to tradition, what are believed to be his remains are held in Santiago de Compostela in Galicia, Spain.

name: Esther
desc: Queen who saved the Jewish people from Haman's plot
wikipedia_summary: Esther, originally Hadassah, is the eponymous heroine of the Book of Esther in the Hebrew Bible.

name: Josiah
desc: Most righteous of Judah's kings; found the book of the law; led the great reformation
wikipedia_summary: Josiah or Yoshiyahu was the 16th king of Judah. Described as "one of Judah’s most important kings," his reign likely marked a turning point in the development of Yahwism.

name: Laman
desc: Elder son of Lehi; rebellious; progenitor of the Lamanites
wikipedia_summary: Lamane or laman means "master of the land" in the Serer language. The name was also sometimes the title of chiefs or kings of the Serer people of the Senegambia region which includes modern day Senegal and the Gambia. This title was also used by some kings of the Wolof kingdoms. The title is sometimes used interchangeably with the old Serer title Maad. After the Guelowars' migration to the Sine and the foundation of the Kingdom of Sine, "lamane" denotes a provincial chief answerable to the King of Sine and Saloum.

name: Mormon
desc: Nephite prophet-historian who abridged the records
wikipedia_summary: Mormons are a religious and cultural group related to Mormonism, the principal branch of the Latter Day Saint movement started by Joseph Smith in upstate New York during the Second Great Awakening. After Smith's death in 1844, the movement split into several groups following different leaders; the majority followed Brigham Young, while smaller groups followed Sidney Rigdon and James Strang. Many who did not follow Young eventually merged into the Community of Christ, led by Smith’s son, Joseph Smith III. The term Mormon typically refers to members of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Sa

name: Simeon
desc: Son of Jacob; tribe later absorbed into Judah
wikipedia_summary: Simeon is a given name, from the Hebrew שמעון, usually transliterated in English as Shimon. In Greek, it is written Συμεών, hence the Latinized spelling Symeon. It is a cognate of the name Simon.

name: Naphtali
desc: Son of Jacob; territory in the north, Galilee region
wikipedia_summary: According to the Book of Genesis, Naphtali was the sixth son of Jacob, the second of his two sons with Bilhah. He was the founder of the Israelite tribe of Naphtali.

name: Mary
desc: Mother of Jesus Christ; favored of God
variants: Mary the mother of the Lord
wikipedia_summary: Mary was a first-century Jewish woman of Nazareth, the wife of Joseph and the mother of Jesus. She is an important figure of Christianity, venerated under various titles such as virgin or queen, many of which are mentioned in the Litany of Loreto. The Eastern and Oriental Orthodox, Catholic, Evangelical Lutheran, Reformed, Anglican, Methodist and Baptist churches believe that Mary, as mother of Jesus, is the Mother of God. The Church of the East historically regarded her as Christotokos, a term still used in the liturgy of the Assyrian Church of the East. She has the highest position in Islam

name: Ahaz
desc: Unfaithful king of Judah; refused to ask a sign from Isaiah
wikipedia_summary: Ahaz an abbreviation of Jehoahaz II, "Yahweh has held" was the twelfth king of Judah, and the son and successor of Jotham. Ahaz was 20 when he became king of Judah and reigned for 16 years.

name: Ruth
desc: Moabitess who remained loyal to Naomi; ancestor of David

name: Zebulun
desc: Son of Jacob; territory bordered the Sea of Galilee
wikipedia_summary: Zebulun was, according to the Books of Genesis and Numbers, the last of the six sons of Jacob and Leah, and the founder of the Israelite tribe of Zebulun. With Leah as a matriarch, biblical scholars believe the tribe to have been regarded by the text's authors as a part of the original Israelite confederation.

name: Oliver Cowdery
desc: Scribe to Joseph Smith; received Aaronic and Melchizedek Priesthood
wikipedia_summary: Oliver H. P. Cowdery was an American religious leader who, with Joseph Smith, was an important participant in the formative period of the Latter Day Saint movement in the 1820s and 1830s.
christ_connection: Oliver Cowdery, as a scribe to Joseph Smith and recipient of the Aaronic and Melchizedek Priesthood, serves as a vital link between the restored gospel and the foundational teachings of Jesus Christ. His role in recording and transmitting the scriptures aligns with the covenantal responsibilities of the priesthood, emphasizing the importance of scriptural fidelity and the transmission of divine revelation. The scriptural authority vested in Cowdery reflects the prophetic role of priesthood holders in preserving and proclaiming the gospel, thereby underscoring the divine commission entrusted to all members of the Church. This connection is further reinforced by the historical context of the Restoration, where the priesthood's role in interpreting and applying scripture becomes a pivotal aspect of the sacred history of Christ.

name: Rehoboam
desc: Son of Solomon; his harshness split the kingdom of Israel
wikipedia_summary: Rehoboam was, according to the Hebrew Bible, the last monarch of the United Kingdom of Israel, though his reign over the unified state was brief; after the Northern and Southern kingdoms were divided, he became the first king of the Kingdom of Judah. He was a son of and the successor to Solomon and a grandson of David.

name: Herod
desc: Ruler who sought to kill the infant Jesus; also Herod Antipas who killed John

name: Issachar
desc: Son of Jacob; tribe settled in Galilee
wikipedia_summary: Issachar was, according to the Book of Genesis, the fifth of the six sons of Jacob and Leah, and the founder of the Israelite Tribe of Issachar. However, some Biblical scholars view this as an eponymous metaphor providing an aetiology of the connectedness of the tribe to others in the Israelite confederation.

name: Asher
desc: Son of Jacob; tribe along the northern coast
wikipedia_summary: Asher, in the Book of Genesis, was the younger of the two sons of Jacob and Zilpah, and Jacob's eighth son overall. He was the founder of the Israelite Tribe of Asher.

name: Caleb
desc: Spy who gave a faithful report; inherited Hebron
wikipedia_summary: Caleb is a figure who appears in the Hebrew Bible as a representative of the Tribe of Judah during the Israelites' journey to the Promised Land.

name: Samson
desc: Judge of Israel; Nazirite of great strength
wikipedia_summary: Samson was the last of the judges of the ancient Israelites mentioned in the Book of Judges and one of the last leaders who "judged" the twelve tribes of Israel before the institution of the monarchy. He is sometimes regarded as an Israelite version of the popular Near Eastern folk hero archetype also embodied by the Sumerian Gilgamesh and Enkidu, as well as the Greek Heracles. Samson was given superhuman powers by God in the form of extreme strength.
christ_connection: Samson, as the judge of Israel and the Nazirite of great strength, points to Jesus Christ through the symbolism of divine deliverance and the fulfillment of the covenant. His miraculous strength and the eventual defeat of the Philistines illustrate the power of the Holy Spirit and the promise of salvation. The narrative of Samson's life, marked by his Nazirite status and eventual redemption, typifies the role of Christ as the ultimate deliverer and the source of spiritual strength, fulfilling the prophecy of the Messiah's anointing and liberation of the people of God. [Judges 13:25][Judges 14:5][Judges 16:23]

name: Ezra
desc: Scribe who led a return from Babylon and restored the law
wikipedia_summary: Ezra is the main character of the Book of Ezra. According to the Hebrew Bible, he was an important Jewish scribe (sofer) and priest (kohen) in the early Second Temple period. In the Greek Septuagint, the name is rendered as Ésdrās, from which the Latin name Esdras comes. His name is probably a shortened Aramaic translation of the Hebrew name עזריהו‎, meaning "Yah helps".

name: Philip
desc: Apostle from Bethsaida; brought Nathanael to Jesus
wikipedia_summary: Philip, also Phillip, is a male name derived from the Greek Φιλιππος, from a compound of φίλος and ἵππος. Prominent Philips who popularized the name include kings of Macedonia and one of the apostles of early Christianity.
christ_connection: Philip, the Apostle from Bethsaida, is depicted as a figure of faith and witness in the Gospels, particularly in [John 1:45-51] where he is called to be the beloved disciple of Jesus. His role in bringing Nathanael to Jesus underscores the theme of divine revelation and the fulfillment of prophecy, as seen in [John 1:48] where Jesus declares, "Believers shall come to me." Philip's ministry exemplifies the covenantal relationship between Jesus and His disciples, and his testimony reflects the typological significance of the apostles as vessels through which God's word is proclaimed. The narrative of Philip's journey highlights the arc of sacred history, wherein the disciples are called to bear witness to the incarnate Word, thereby connecting to the eternal covenant of salvation.

name: Sam
desc: Son of Lehi; followed Nephi in faithfulness

name: Micah
desc: Prophet who foretold the birth of Christ in Bethlehem
wikipedia_summary: Micah is a given name.

name: Judas Iscariot
desc: Apostle who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver; fulfilled prophecy of Zechariah
wikipedia_summary: Judas Iscariot was, according to Christianity's four canonical gospels, one of the original Twelve Apostles of Jesus Christ. Judas betrayed Jesus to the Sanhedrin in the Garden of Gethsemane in exchange for thirty pieces of silver, by kissing him on the cheek and addressing him as "master" to reveal his identity to the crowd who had come to arrest him. In modern times, his name is often used synonymously with betrayal or treason.

name: Abinadi
desc: Prophet martyred by fire; testimony converted Alma; prophesied of Christ
wikipedia_summary: According to the Book of Mormon, Abinadi was a prophet who lived on the American continent about 150 BC. In the Book of Mormon account, Abinadi visited the court of King Noah at Lehi-Nephi, and pleaded for them to repent of their iniquity and live the law of Moses. Abinadi also gave Noah the message of the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ to earth in the flesh, to live among the children of men. Noah and his priests threatened Abinadi that unless he recalled all the words he had said against him and his priests, they would kill him. Abinadi stood by his words and Noah had him burned with fire.

name: Pahoran
desc: Chief judge of the Nephites during Moroni's wars; received the famous epistle of Captain Moroni

name: Teancum
desc: Nephite military commander; killed Amalickiah and Ammoron; died defending his people
wikipedia_summary: According to the Book of Mormon, Teancum was a Nephite military leader. He is described in the Book of Alma between Alma 50:35 and Alma 62:40 (inclusive). According to LDS teachings, he is known for the assassinations of King Amalickiah and the subsequent assassination of Amalickiah's brother, Ammoron, seven years later. The Book of Mormon states that in time he proved to be a great chief captain in the Nephite army.
christ_connection: Teancum, as a Nephite military commander, exemplifies the virtues of courage, leadership, and divine purpose, which are essential qualities for a leader guided by the principles of the gospel. His actions, particularly in the Book of Mormon, reflect the covenantal relationship between God and His people, as he defends his community against external threats, thereby illustrating the fulfillment of prophetic promises. Teancum's legacy is intertwined with the broader narrative of salvation, where his deeds typify the ultimate sacrifice and victory of Christ, who is both the fulfillment of the covenant and the embodiment of the divine plan for humanity. His story underscores the importance of faith, obedience, and the role of the church in preserving the covenant through the faithful stewardship of the saints.

name: Gedaliah
desc: Governor appointed by Babylon over Judah after the destruction of Jerusalem
wikipedia_summary: Gedaliah was a person from the Bible who was a governor of Yehud province. He was also the son of Ahikam, who saved the prophet Jeremiah.
christ_connection: Gedaliah, the governor of Judah appointed by Babylon following the destruction of Jerusalem, serves as a type of Christ, reflecting the structure of the covenant and the sacrificial nature of leadership in times of divine judgment. His appointment by Babylon, a foreign power, parallels the role of Christ, who was appointed by God to restore the covenant relationship between God and His people. The fate of Gedaliah, who was killed by the Babylonians, typifies the eventual rejection of Christ by the religious leaders of the time, illustrating the theme of sacrificial obedience and the consequences of spiritual complacency. The covenantal relationship established by Gedaliah, though broken, underscores the enduring nature of the covenantal promises, which are ultimately fulfilled in Christ.

name: Rebekah
desc: Wife of Isaac; mother of Jacob and Esau
christ_connection: Rebekah, as the wife of Isaac and mother of Jacob and Esau, serves as a typological figure in the Old Testament, emblematic of the Virgin Mary, the mother of Jesus Christ. Her covenantal relationship with Isaac mirrors the covenantal relationship between God and Jesus, emphasizing faith, obedience, and the fulfillment of divine promises. The narrative of Rebekah's journey, marked by trials and divine intervention, parallels the spiritual journey of Mary, who is portrayed as theantity of Christ, through whom God's redemptive plan is enacted. The scriptural reference [Genesis 24:66] underscores her role in the divine arrangement, reflecting the pre-incarnate nature of Christ and the fulfillment of God's covenantal purposes.

name: Lemuel
desc: Son of Lehi; followed Laman in rebellion
wikipedia_summary: Lemuel is a Hebrew name, meaning "devoted to God", which may refer to:

name: Ether
desc: Last Jaredite prophet; wrote the Jaredite record sealed to Moroni
wikipedia_summary: In organic chemistry, ethers are a class of compounds that contain an ether group, a single oxygen atom bonded to two separate carbon atoms, each part of an organyl group. They have the general formula R−O−R′, where R and R′ represent the organyl groups. Ethers can again be classified into two varieties: if the organyl groups are the same on both sides of the oxygen atom, then it is a simple or symmetrical ether, whereas if they are different, the ethers are called mixed or unsymmetrical ethers. A typical example of the first group is the solvent and anaesthetic diethyl ether, commonly referre

name: Melchizedek
desc: King of Salem; priest of the Most High God; type of Christ; the higher priesthood bears his name
wikipedia_summary: In the Hebrew Bible, Melchizedek was the king of Salem and priest of El Elyon. He is mentioned in Genesis 14:18–20, where he brings out bread and wine and blesses Abram (Abraham), following the Battle of the Vale of Siddim and Abram's subsequent rescue of the captives and plunder taken in the battle, and in Psalm 110:4.
christ_connection: Melchizedek, a figure in the Old Testament, is designated as a type of Christ, as he embodies the priesthood of Christ and the blessing of God upon the righteous. His elevation by Abraham and the distribution of the tithes signify the establishment of a new covenant, wherein the priesthood is not bound by the Levitical system but is instead instituted by God Himself. This is mirrored in Christ, who, as the eternal High Priest, offers a superior sacrifice and bestows eternal redemption upon the elect. [Hebrews 7:1-3]

name: Gadianton
desc: Founder of the secret combination that plagued Nephite society for centuries
wikipedia_summary: The Gadianton robbers, according to the Book of Mormon, were a secret criminal organization in ancient America. Their use of murder and plunder to destabilize society and overthrow the extant government makes them similar to the Sicarii.

name: Barnabas
desc: Companion of Paul; son of consolation
wikipedia_summary: Barnabas, born Joseph (Ἰωσήφ) or Joses (Ἰωσής), was a prominent Christian disciple, identified as an apostle in Acts 14:14. According to Acts 4:36, he was a Cypriot Levite. He undertook missionary journeys as a companion of Paul the Apostle, evangelizing among the "God-fearing" Gentiles who attended synagogues in some of the Hellenized cities of Anatolia. He participated in the Council of Jerusalem.

name: Zeezrom
desc: Lawyer who challenged Alma and Amulek; converted and healed; became a missionary
wikipedia_summary: In the Book of Mormon, Zeezrom is a Nephite lawyer who, through deceit and money, seeks to gain power among the Nephites through his vocation. Alma the Younger and his missionary companion Amulek teach Zeezrom in Ammonihah. At first he resists, but is ultimately converted to the Nephite religion.

name: Timothy
desc: Young companion and protégé of Paul
christ_connection: Timothy, as a young companion and protégé of Paul, serves as a typological figure within the narrative of the New Testament, emblematic of the faithful disciple who is called to preach the Gospel and uphold the teachings of Christ. His role is both a covenantal promise and a prophetic anticipation, reflecting the divine purpose of the Church in the midst of the world. Timothy's ministry is a testament to the continuity of the gospel, bridging the Old and New Testaments through the lens of covenantal fidelity and the prophetic call to spiritual leadership. [Acts 14:21-22][1 Timothy 1:1-2]

name: Jephthah
desc: Judge who delivered Israel from Ammon; made a rash vow
wikipedia_summary: Jephthah appears in the Book of Judges as a judge who presided over Israel for a period of six years. According to Judges, he lived in Gilead. His father's name is also given as Gilead, and, as his mother is described as a prostitute, this may indicate that his father might have been any of the men of that area. Jephthah led the Israelites in battle against Ammon and, in exchange for defeating the Ammonites, made a vow to sacrifice whatever would come out of the door of his house first. When his daughter was the first to come out of the house, he immediately regretted the vow, which bound him

name: Uriah
desc: Hittite soldier; faithful husband of Bathsheba; killed by David's arrangement

name: Ham
desc: Son of Noah; ancestor of the Hamitic peoples
wikipedia_summary: Ham is pork from a leg cut that has been preserved by wet or dry curing, with or without smoking. As a processed meat, the term ham includes both whole cuts of meat and ones that have been mechanically formed.
christ_connection: [Genesis 5:3-5] Ham's lineage is traced in the genealogy of Christ, as the progenitor of the Hamitic peoples, who are foretold in the covenant of grace. The covenantal relationship between Ham and the divine promises of the New Covenant are parallel, with Ham representing the initial covenantal seed and Christ the culmination of the covenantal promise. The typological significance of Ham lies in his role as the progenitor of a people whose destiny is fulfilled in the Christ of the New Covenant, thus linking the Old and New Testaments through the covenantal structure.

name: Phinehas
desc: Son of Eleazar; his zeal in stopping Israel's apostasy stayed the plague
wikipedia_summary: According to the Hebrew Bible, Phinehas was a priest during the Exodus. The grandson of Aaron and son of Eleazar, the High Priests, he distinguished himself as a youth at Shittim with his zeal against the heresy of Peor.

name: Hyrum Smith
desc: Brother of Joseph Smith; martyred at Carthage Jail
wikipedia_summary: Hyrum Smith was an American religious leader in the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints, the original church of the Latter Day Saint movement. He was the older brother of the movement's founder, Joseph Smith, and was killed with his brother at Carthage Jail where they were being held awaiting trial.

name: Enosh
desc: Son of Seth; in his time men began to call upon the name of the Lord

name: Shem
desc: Son of Noah; ancestor of the Semitic peoples; identified with Melchizedek in some traditions
wikipedia_summary: Shem is one of the sons of Noah in the Bible.

name: Boaz
desc: Kinsman-redeemer who married Ruth; ancestor of David and of Christ; type of the Redeemer
wikipedia_summary: Boaz is a biblical figure appearing in the Book of Ruth in the Hebrew Bible and in the genealogies of Jesus in the New Testament and also the name of a pillar in the portico of the historic Temple in Jerusalem. The word is found 24 times in the Scriptures, two being in Greek.

name: Shiz
desc: Jaredite military leader; last enemy of Coriantumr; killed in the final battle
wikipedia_summary: In the Book of Mormon, Shiz is a Jaredite military leader who was beheaded by Coriantumr. Since the nineteenth century, the account of Shiz's death in the Book of Ether has been claimed by critics to be an error in the Book of Mormon.

name: Joel
desc: Prophet whose words Peter cited at Pentecost; foretold the outpouring of the Spirit

name: Jethro
desc: Priest of Midian; father-in-law of Moses; advised Moses on governance
wikipedia_summary: Jethro is a male given name meaning "excellence". It is derived from the Hebrew word Yithrô.

name: Naomi
desc: Mother-in-law of Ruth; her story frames covenant loyalty across nations

name: Jezebel
desc: Phoenician wife of Ahab; promoted Baal worship; persecuted the prophets
wikipedia_summary: Jezebel was the daughter of Ithobaal I of Tyre and the wife of Ahab, King of Israel, according to the Book of Kings of the Hebrew Bible.

name: Thomas
desc: Apostle; doubted then testified of the risen Christ

name: Obadiah
desc: Shortest prophetic book; prophesied against Edom
wikipedia_summary: Obadiah, also known as Abdias, is a biblical prophet. The authorship of the Book of Obadiah is traditionally attributed to the prophet Obadiah.

name: Morianton
desc: Leader who fled with his people to the north; stopped by Teancum
wikipedia_summary: This list is intended as a compendium of individuals mentioned in the Book of Mormon.

name: Amos
desc: Prophet who cried for justice and righteousness

name: Jonah
desc: Prophet sent to Nineveh; sign of Christ's burial and resurrection
wikipedia_summary: Jonah the son of Amittai or Jonas was a Jewish prophet from Gath-hepher in the Northern Kingdom of Israel around the 8th century BCE according to the Hebrew Bible. He is the central figure of the Book of Jonah, one of the minor prophets, which details his reluctance in delivering the judgment of God to the city of Nineveh in the Neo-Assyrian Empire. After he is swallowed by a large sea creature and then released, he returns to the divine mission.

name: Silas
desc: Companion of Paul; imprisoned and sang hymns with Paul at Philippi
wikipedia_summary: Silas or Silvanus was a leading member of the Early Christian community, who according to the New Testament accompanied Paul the Apostle on his second missionary journey.

name: Akish
desc: Jaredite king who established secret combinations; brought the kingdom to ruin
wikipedia_summary: This list is intended as a compendium of individuals mentioned in the Book of Mormon.

name: Antipus
desc: Nephite commander who fought alongside Helaman's stripling warriors; died in battle
