wikipedia_summary: This list is intended as a compendium of individuals mentioned in the Book of Mormon.

name: Eve
desc: First woman; mother of all living
wikipedia_summary: Eve is a figure from the Book of Genesis in the Hebrew Bible. According to the origin story of the Abrahamic religions, she was the first woman to be created by God. Eve is known also as Adam's wife.

name: Methuselah
desc: Son of Enoch; lived 969 years, the oldest man recorded in scripture
wikipedia_summary: Methuselah was a biblical patriarch and a figure in Judaism, Christianity, and Islam. He is claimed to have lived the longest life, dying at 969 years of age. According to the Book of Genesis, Methuselah was the son of Enoch, the father of Lamech, and the grandfather of Noah. Elsewhere in the Bible, Methuselah is mentioned in genealogies in 1 Chronicles and the Gospel of Luke.

name: Lazarus
desc: Raised from the dead by Jesus; brother of Mary and Martha

name: Kishkumen
desc: Murderer of Pahoran II; co-founder of the Gadianton robbers
wikipedia_summary: The Gadianton robbers, according to the Book of Mormon, were a secret criminal organization in ancient America. Their use of murder and plunder to destabilize society and overthrow the extant government makes them similar to the Sicarii.
christ_connection: Kishkumen, as a figure in the Book of Mormon, serves as a typological precursor to Jesus Christ, embodying the moral and spiritual corruption that precedes the coming of the Messiah. His role as a murderer of Pahoran II reflects the antithesis of Christ's mission to redeem and restore righteousness. The narrative of Kishkumen's actions parallels the broader theme of divine judgment and the necessity of a Redeemer, which is fulfilled in Jesus Christ. The Book of Mormon's depiction of Kishkumen underscores the covenantal relationship between God and His people, illustrating how the law is broken and the promise of salvation is introduced through the coming of Christ.

name: Japheth
desc: Son of Noah; ancestor of the Gentile nations
wikipedia_summary: Japheth was one of the three sons of Noah in the Book of Genesis. In the biblical narrative he plays a role in the story of Noah's drunkenness and the curse of Ham, and subsequently in the Table of Nations, he is named as the ancestor of the peoples of the Aegean Sea, Anatolia, Caucasus, Greece, and elsewhere in Eurasia.
christ_connection: Japheth, as the son of Noah and the ancestor of the Gentile nations, points to Jesus Christ through the covenantal lineage established in the Book of Genesis. His progeny, including the nations of Canaan, Ephraim, and Judah, are typified in the covenantal promises made to Abraham and Isaac, foreshadowing the fulfillment of the New Covenant through Christ. The narrative of Japheth's descendants underscores the universal call of God to all peoples, reflecting the inclusive nature of the Gospel and the role of Jesus as the Messiah who brings salvation to all nations. [Genesis 10:11-12; 12:1-3]

name: Titus
desc: Companion of Paul; leader of the church in Crete
wikipedia_summary: Titus Flavius Vespasianus was Roman emperor from 79 to 81 AD. A member of the Flavian dynasty, Titus succeeded his father Vespasian upon his death, becoming the first Roman emperor ever to succeed his biological father.
christ_connection: [Titus 1:3] Titus, as a companion of Paul and leader of the church in Crete, exemplifies the covenantal fidelity required of believers, reflecting the divine promise of Christ's salvation. His role in pastoral leadership parallels the ministry of Christ, who instituted the church and entrusted its care to His disciples. The structure of Titus's epistle, with its emphasis on doctrine and moral conduct, mirrors the doctrinal framework of Christ's teachings, illustrating the continuity between the Old and New Testament. Thus, Titus serves as a typological figure, prefigured in the covenantal promises of Christ, and typified in the moral and spiritual standards of the Church.

name: Amlici
desc: Follower of Nehor who sought to be king; defeated by Alma; allied with Lamanites
wikipedia_summary: According to the Book of Mormon, the Amlicites were a break-off group of Nephites in the Book of Alma, around 87 B.C. Their leader, Amlici, is not chosen by the people as king, so he and the Amlicites leave the Nephites and join the Lamanites. The Nephites win both of their battles with the Amlicites and Alma kills Amlici in the second battle.

name: Lib
desc: Mighty Jaredite hunter and king who preserved the wilderness for game
christ_connection: [Genesis 1:28] Lib is depicted as a mighty Jaredite hunter and king who preserved the wilderness for game, reflecting the covenantal role of a leader who safeguards the sacred space of nature for the benefit of the people. This imagery parallels the sacred history of Jesus Christ, who, as the Lamb of God, preserves the covenant of grace through His sacrifice, sustaining the spiritual life of the faithful. The typological connection lies in the idea of stewardship and preservation, which are central to both Lib's role and Jesus' ministry, where the latter sustains the spiritual inheritance of the elect.

name: Miriam
desc: Sister of Moses; prophetess of Israel
wikipedia_summary: Miriam is described in the Hebrew Bible as the daughter of Amram and Jochebed, and the older sister of Moses and Aaron. She was a prophetess and first appears in the Book of Exodus.

name: Nehemiah
desc: Governor who rebuilt the walls of Jerusalem after the exile
wikipedia_summary: Nehemiah is the central figure of the Book of Nehemiah, which describes his work in rebuilding Jerusalem during the Second Temple period as the governor of Yehud Medinata, the autonomous province of Judea within the Achaemenid Empire, under Artaxerxes I.

name: Hagar
desc: Egyptian handmaid of Sarah; mother of Ishmael; angel ministered to her twice
wikipedia_summary: According to the Book of Genesis, Hagar is an Egyptian slave, a handmaiden of Sarah, whom Sarah gave to her own husband Abram as a wife to bear him a child. Abraham's firstborn son through Hagar, Ishmael, became the progenitor of the Ishmaelites, generally taken to be the Arabs. Various commentators have connected her to the Hagrites, perhaps claiming her as their eponymous ancestor. Hagar is alluded to, although not named, in the Quran, and Islam considers her Abraham's second wife.

name: Andrew
desc: Apostle; brother of Peter; first called
wikipedia_summary: Andrew is the English form from the Old French name Andreu / Andrieu, themselves from Latin Andreas, from Greek-derived given name Andreas. It is related to Ancient Greek: ἀνήρ/ἀνδρός aner/andros, "man", thus meaning "manly" and, as consequence, "brave", "strong", "courageous", and "warrior". In the King James Bible, the Greek "Ἀνδρέας" is translated as Andrew.

name: Martha
desc: Sister of Mary and Lazarus; received testimony of the Resurrection
wikipedia_summary: Martha is a biblical figure described in the Gospels of Luke and John. Together with her siblings Lazarus and Mary of Bethany, she is described as living in the village of Bethany near Jerusalem and witnessing Jesus resurrecting her brother, Lazarus.

name: Zacharias
desc: Priest; father of John the Baptist; struck dumb for disbelieving Gabriel's message
wikipedia_summary: Zechariah was a Jewish priest mentioned in the New Testament and as a prophet in the Quran, and venerated in Christianity and Islam. In the Bible, he is the father of John the Baptist, a priest of the sons of Aaron in the Gospel of Luke, and the husband of Elizabeth who is a relative of the Virgin Mary. In the Quran, his story is mentioned in the initial verse of surah Maryam.

name: Brother of Jared
desc: Powerful prophet; saw the finger of God; shown all things
wikipedia_summary: In the Book of Mormon, the Brother of Jared is the most prominent person in the account given in the beginning of the Book of Ether. The Brother of Jared's name is not given in the text of the Book of Mormon, but Joseph Smith stated in 1834 that it was Mahonri Moriancumer.

name: Korihor
desc: Anti-Christ who denied Christ; struck dumb by God; trampled to death among the Zoramites
christ_connection: Korihor, as an anti-Christ figure in the Book of Mormon, serves as a typological precursor to Jesus Christ, embodying the characteristics of a false prophet and a rebellious leader who rejects the divine covenant. His denial of Christ and subsequent trampling to death among the Zoramites reflect the broader theme of sacrificial rejection of the Messiah, a motif that parallels the crucifixion of Jesus Christ. The divine punishment inflicted upon Korihor, as described in [2 Nephi 25:18], underscores the divine justice and the ultimate triumph of Christ over spiritual adversaries, thus linking Korihor to the broader narrative of salvation and the fulfillment of prophecies concerning the Messiah.

name: Hannah
desc: Mother of Samuel; her prayer is a model of faith
christ_connection: Hannah's prayer, recorded in [1 Samuel 1:11], exemplifies the depth of faith required in the covenant of grace, as she trusts in God's promise despite the apparent abandonment of her son, Samuel, by his father David. This prayer typifies the faithful reliance on divine sovereignty, a theme central to the covenantal relationship between God and His people. The narrative of Hannah's devotion connects to Jesus Christ through the fulfillment of the covenantal promise, as the New Testament portrays Hannah as a precursor to the Virgin Mary, whose faith and obedience mirror the spiritual character of Christ. The covenantal context of Hannah's story, rooted in the Old Testament, anticipates the redemptive work of Jesus, who embodies the culmination of the covenantal purpose and the fulfillment of the promises made to Israel.

name: Rahab
desc: Canaanite woman of Jericho who hid the spies; saved by the scarlet thread; ancestor of Christ
wikipedia_summary: Rahab was a prostitute from Jericho during the Israelite conquest of Canaan. In the Book of Joshua of the Hebrew Bible, she is credited with aiding the Israelites by hiding two spies who had been sent by Joshua to scout the city before the Israelite assault. Her actions led to the fall of Jericho, during which Israelite fighters killed every Canaanite inhabitant of the city.

name: Bathsheba
desc: Wife of Uriah; taken by David; mother of Solomon; in the lineage of Christ
wikipedia_summary: Bathsheba was an Israelite queen consort. According to the Hebrew Bible, she was the wife of Uriah the Hittite and later of David, with whom she had all of her five children. Her status as the mother of Solomon, who succeeded David as monarch, made her the Gebirah (גְּבִירָה) of the Kingdom of Israel.

name: Zephaniah
desc: Prophet of Josiah's era; declared the day of the Lord
wikipedia_summary: Zephaniah is the name of several people in the Hebrew Bible; the most prominent being the prophet who prophesied in the days of Josiah, king of Judah and is attributed a book bearing his name among the Twelve Minor Prophets. His name is commonly transliterated Sophonias in Bibles translated from the Vulgate or Septuagint. The name might mean "Yahweh has hidden/protected," or "Yah lies in wait". The church father Jerome interpreted the name to mean "the watchman of the Lord".

name: Haggai
desc: Post-exile prophet who urged the rebuilding of the temple
wikipedia_summary: Haggai or Aggeus was a Hebrew prophet active during the building of the Second Temple in Jerusalem, one of the twelve minor prophets in the Hebrew Bible, and the author or subject of the Book of Haggai. He is known for his prophecy in 520 BCE, commanding the Jews to rebuild the Temple. He was the first of three post-exilic prophets from the Neo-Babylonian Exile of the House of Judah, who belonged to the period of Jewish history which began after the return from captivity in Babylon. His name means "my holidays".

name: Nathanael
desc: Apostle in whom there was no guile; also called Bartholomew
wikipedia_summary: Nathanael is an English name of Hebrew origin. It is of Biblical origin and holds significance for Jews and Christians. Several figures in both the Old and New Testament bear the name. Figures in the Old Testament, which is transliterated from Hebrew, have their names rendered as Nethanel in English whereas those in the New Testament, which is translated from Greek, have theirs rendered as Nathanael. Since the early 20th century, the most common English spelling is Nathaniel, a change likely influenced by the popularity of other Biblical names ending in -iel. Bearers may use the nicknames Nate

name: Apollos
desc: Eloquent Jewish teacher; instructed in the way of the Lord by Priscilla and Aquila
wikipedia_summary: Apollos was a 1st-century Alexandrian Jewish Christian mentioned several times in the New Testament. A contemporary and colleague of Paul the Apostle, he played an important role in the early development of the churches of Ephesus and Corinth.

name: Nehor
desc: Taught priestcraft; killed Gideon; his order led to great wickedness among the Nephites
wikipedia_summary: Nehor is the founder of an apostate sect mentioned in the Book of Mormon around 90 BC in the first year of the reign of the judges. He teaches the Nephites that priests and teachers should be supported by their followers, and that all will be saved in the end. Nehor is brought before Alma the Younger for killing Gideon, a Nephite elder who argued with him. Alma accuses him of priestcraft and sentences him to death for enforcing his beliefs with violence. When executed, Nehor admits to teaching against the word of God.

name: Deborah
desc: Judge and prophetess of Israel
wikipedia_summary: According to the Book of Judges, Deborah was a prophetess of Judaism, the fourth Judge of pre-monarchic Israel and the only female judge mentioned in the Hebrew Bible. Many scholars contend that the phrase, "a woman of Lappidoth", as translated from biblical Hebrew in Judges 4:4 denotes her marital status as the wife of Lapidoth. Alternatively, "lappid" translates as "torch" or "lightning", therefore the phrase, "woman of Lappidoth" could be referencing Deborah as a "fiery woman". Deborah told Barak, an Israelite general from Kedesh in Naphtali, that God commanded him to lead an attack against

name: Ezekiel
desc: Prophet among the exiles in Babylon; vision of the valley of dry bones
wikipedia_summary: Ezekiel, also spelled Ezechiel, was an Israelite priest. The Book of Ezekiel, relating his visions and acts, is named after him.

name: Malachi
desc: Last Old Testament prophet; prophesied Elijah's return
wikipedia_summary: Malachi or Malachias is the name used by the author of the Book of Malachi, the last book of the Nevi'im (Prophets) section of the Tanakh. It is possible that Malachi is not a proper name, because it means "messenger"; it has been assumed to be a pseudonym. According to Jewish tradition, Malachi's true identity is Ezra the scribe.

name: Cornelius
desc: Roman centurion; first Gentile baptized; received the Holy Ghost before baptism

name: Ananias
desc: Disciple in Damascus sent by the Lord to restore Saul's sight after his vision

name: Zoram
desc: Servant of Laban who joined Lehi's family and was a free man

name: Hosea
desc: Prophet whose marriage symbolized God's covenant with Israel
wikipedia_summary: In the Hebrew Bible, Hosea, also known as Osee, son of Beeri, was an 8th-century BC prophet in Israel and the nominal primary author of the Book of Hosea. He is the first of the Twelve Minor Prophets, whose collective writings were aggregated and organized into a single book in the Jewish Tanakh by the Second Temple period but which are distinguished as individual books in Christianity. Hosea is often seen as a "prophet of doom", but underneath his message of destruction is a promise of restoration. The Talmud claims that he was the greatest prophet of his generation. The period of Hosea's min

name: Ehud
desc: Second judge; left-handed deliverer who slew Eglon king of Moab
wikipedia_summary: Ehud ben‑Gera is described in the biblical Book of Judges chapter 3 as a judge who was sent by God to deliver the Israelites from Moabite domination. He is described as being left-handed and a member of the Tribe of Benjamin.

name: Stephen
desc: First Christian martyr; saw Christ at the right hand of God
wikipedia_summary: Stephen or Steven is an English male first name. It is particularly significant to Christians, as it belonged to Saint Stephen, an early disciple and deacon who, according to the Book of Acts, was stoned to death; he is widely regarded as the first martyr of the Christian Church.

name: Caiaphas
desc: High priest who condemned Jesus
wikipedia_summary: Joseph ben Caiaphas was the High Priest of Israel during the first century. In the New Testament, the Gospels of Matthew, Luke and John indicate he was an organizer of the plot to kill Jesus. He is portrayed as presiding over the Sanhedrin trial of Jesus. The primary sources for Caiaphas' life are the New Testament and the writings of Josephus. The latter records he was made high priest by the Roman procurator Valerius Gratus after Simon ben Camithus had been deposed.

name: Elisabeth
desc: Wife of Zacharias; mother of John the Baptist; filled with the Holy Ghost at Mary's greeting

name: Zeniff
desc: Leader of the Nephite colony who returned to the land of Nephi; over-zealous for inheritance
wikipedia_summary: Zeniff is a king in the Book of Mormon whose personal account is recorded in the Book of Mosiah. He is the father of King Noah and the grandfather of King Limhi. Zeniff is the first king of Nephite colonists who come from Zarahemla and settle in the land of Lehi-Nephi. The Nephites believe this land to be rightfully theirs by inheritance, even attempting to reclaim the land by force. In an expedition in which he spies for the Nephites, Zeniff claims to see good in the Lamanite inhabitants. He argues against a militaristic approach and causes an internal battle among the Nephite army. Zeniff la

name: Achan
desc: Man of Judah who took forbidden spoils at Jericho; brought defeat on Israel
christ_connection: Achan's actions at Jericho, where he took forbidden spoils and thereby brought defeat upon Israel, typify the sin of idolatry and the consequence of disobedience to God's covenant. His story is recorded in [Joshua 7:1-11], and it serves as a warning against the corruption of the covenant and the dangers of pride and greed. The narrative connects to Jesus Christ through the theme of sacrificial atonement and the fulfillment of the covenantal promise that those who reject God will face judgment, as seen in [Hebrews 10:29]. Achan's fate parallels the fate of the unrepentant sinner, reflecting the broader theological trajectory of the Old Testament leading toward the New Covenant and the ultimate sacrifice of Christ.

name: Othniel
desc: First judge of Israel; nephew of Caleb; delivered Israel from Mesopotamia
wikipedia_summary: Othniel was the first of the biblical judges. The etymology of his name is uncertain, but may mean "God/He is my strength" or "God has helped me".

name: Priscilla
desc: Co-worker with Paul; with Aquila taught Apollos; hosted a church in her house
wikipedia_summary: Priscilla is an English female given name adopted from Latin Prisca, derived from priscus.

name: Aquila
desc: Tentmaker; husband of Priscilla; faithful companion of Paul
christ_connection: Aquila, as a tentmaker, typifies the role of a prophet and a shepherd, reflecting the ministry of Jesus who tended to the spiritual needs of his followers. His faithfulness in accompanying Paul, a apostle, underscores the importance of companionship and spiritual guidance in the early Christian community, mirroring the relationship between Jesus and his disciples. The covenantal relationship established between Aquila and Priscilla, as recorded in [Acts 18:2-3], parallels the divine covenant between God and His people, illustrating how the faithful servants of the gospel are called to uphold and proclaim the Word of God, much as Jesus Himself was entrusted with the mission of spreading the Gospel.

name: Riplakish
desc: Wicked Jaredite king who taxed his people and enslaved them to build buildings
wikipedia_summary: This list is intended as a compendium of individuals mentioned in the Book of Mormon.
christ_connection: Riplakish, the wicked Jaredite king, serves as a typological figure within the Book of Mormon, illustrating the consequences of divine judgment and the rejection of divine covenant. His taxation and enslavement of his people mirror the spiritual and moral failings of the Israelites under Moses, reflecting the broader theme of divine punishment for disobedience. The narrative of Riplakish parallels the historical context of Jesus Christ, who similarly confronted religious corruption and sought to restore the covenant through repentance and spiritual renewal. Thus, Riplakish typifies the role of a king who forsakes divine will, foreshadowing the eventual redemption of the covenant through Christ's atoning sacrifice.

name: Nicodemus
desc: Pharisee who came to Jesus by night; learned of being born again
wikipedia_summary: Nicodemus is a New Testament figure venerated as a saint in a number of Christian traditions. He is depicted as a Pharisee and a member of the Sanhedrin who is drawn to hear Jesus's teachings. Like Lazarus, Nicodemus is not mentioned in the synoptic Gospels, but only by John, who devotes more than half of Chapter 3 of his gospel and a few verses of Chapter 7 to Nicodemus; and, lastly, mentions him in Chapter 19.
christ_connection: Nicodemus, a Pharisee who came to Jesus by night, is typified by the process of spiritual rebirth and is thus a prefiguration of the Christian experience of being born again. His journey reflects the covenantal promise of salvation through faith, as he sought understanding of the divine nature of Jesus, and is thus connected to the doctrine of the new birth and the work of the Holy Spirit. [John 3:1-21] [John 3:30]

name: Emma Smith
desc: Wife of Joseph Smith; first president of Relief Society
wikipedia_summary: Emma Hale Smith Bidamon was a leader in the early Latter Day Saint movement and a prominent member of the Reorganized Church of Jesus Christ of Latter Day Saints as well as the first wife of Joseph Smith, the movement's founder. In 1842, when the Ladies' Relief Society of Nauvoo was formed as a women's service organization, she was elected by its members as the organization's first president.
christ_connection: Emma Smith, as the first president of the Relief Society and wife of Joseph Smith, serves as a typological figure within the broader context of the covenantal relationship between God and His people. Her role in the restoration of the gospel aligns with the prophetic function of the priesthood and the establishment of the Church, as seen in [Book of Mormon:1:3]. Her dedication to the cause of Christ and her leadership in the early Church reflect the covenantal promises made to the prophets, particularly in the context of the Book of Mormon and the Book of Revelation. Emma Smith's life and work exemplify the doctrine of the priesthood and the importance of spiritual leadership, which are central to the restoration of the gospel and the fulfillment of divine prophecies.

name: Sariah
desc: Wife of Lehi; mother of Nephi; murmured then believed
wikipedia_summary: According to the Book of Mormon, Sariah was the wife of Lehi, and the mother of Laman, Lemuel, Sam, and Nephi. She traveled with her husband from Jerusalem, into the wilderness, and eventually, across the ocean to the "promised land". She is noted for the story in First Nephi where she complains to Lehi for sending her sons back to Jerusalem thinking that they may have died. Once they return, Sariah testifies that her husband is truly a prophet. In Lehi's vision of the tree of life, Sariah chooses to eat the fruit representing God's love. She has two more sons, Jacob and Joseph, while travelin

name: Habakkuk
desc: Prophet who questioned God's justice; answered with the vision of faith
wikipedia_summary: Habakkuk, or Habacuc, who was active around 612 BC, was a prophet whose oracles and prayer are recorded in the Book of Habakkuk, the eighth of the collected twelve minor prophets in the Hebrew Bible. He is revered by Jews, Christians, and Muslims.

name: Zacchaeus
desc: Chief publican who climbed a tree to see Jesus
wikipedia_summary: Zacchaeus was a man, recorded in the Gospel of Luke, a chief tax-collector at Jericho. His story includes his faith in climbing a sycamore tree to see Jesus and also his generosity in giving away half of all he possessed.

name: Lydia
desc: Seller of purple in Philippi; first European convert; hosted Paul's missionary work
wikipedia_summary: Lydia was an Iron Age kingdom situated in western Anatolia, in modern-day Turkey. Later, it became an important province of the Achaemenid Empire and then the Roman Empire. Its capital was Sardis.

name: Dorcas
desc: Disciple of Joppa raised from the dead by Peter; known for charitable works
wikipedia_summary: Dorcas, or Tabitha, was an early disciple of Jesus mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles. She lived in the port city of Joppa, today absorbed by Tel Aviv. Acts describes her as being known for her "good works and acts of mercy", sewing clothes for the poor. When she died, the widows of her community mourned her and sent urgently for Peter, who was in nearby Lydda. As evidence of her charity, they showed him some of the clothes she had sewn, and according to the biblical account he raised her from the dead.

name: Corianton
desc: Son of Alma; left his mission for Isabel; received Alma's profound discourse on resurrection and justice

name: Brigham Young
desc: Second prophet; led pioneer exodus to Utah; colonized the West
wikipedia_summary: Brigham Young was an American religious leader and politician. He was the second president of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints from 1847 until his death in 1877. He also served as the first governor of the Utah Territory from 1851 until his resignation in 1858.

name: Nahum
desc: Prophet who foretold the destruction of Nineveh
wikipedia_summary: Nahum was a minor prophet whose prophecy is recorded in the Tanakh, also called the Hebrew Bible and the Old Testament. His book comes in chronological order between Micah and Habakkuk in the Bible. He wrote about the end of the Assyrian Empire, and its capital city, Nineveh, in a vivid poetic style.

name: Thaddaeus
desc: Apostle; also called Lebbaeus and Judas son of James
wikipedia_summary: Jude the Apostle was one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus according to the New Testament. He is generally identified as Thaddeus and is also variously called Judas Thaddaeus, Jude Thaddaeus, Jude of James, or Lebbaeus. He is sometimes identified with Jude, the brother of Jesus, but is clearly distinguished from Judas Iscariot, the disciple who betrayed Jesus prior to his crucifixion. name: Matthias
desc: Chosen by lot to replace Judas Iscariot among the Twelve
wikipedia_summary: Matthias is a name derived from the Greek Ματθαίος, in origin similar to Matthew.

name: Agabus
desc: Prophet who foretold the famine and Paul's imprisonment in Jerusalem
wikipedia_summary: Agabus was an early follower of Christianity from Syria mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles as a prophet. He is traditionally remembered as one of the Seventy Disciples described in Luke 10.

name: Sherem
desc: Anti-Christ who confronted Jacob and was struck by God
wikipedia_summary: This list is intended as a compendium of individuals mentioned in the Book of Mormon.

name: Aminadi
desc: Ancestor of Amulek; descendant of Nephi; interpreted the writing on the temple wall
wikipedia_summary: This list is intended as a compendium of individuals mentioned in the Book of Mormon.
christ_connection: Aminadi, as an ancestor of Amulek and descendant of Nephi, is emblematic of the lineage of prophets foretold in the Book of Mormon, reflecting the covenantal relationship between God and His people. His interpretation of the writing on the temple wall, a symbolic act of divine revelation, parallels the prophetic function of Jesus Christ, who is both the fulfillment of ancient prophecies and the ultimate interpreter of divine will. The role of Aminadi in revealing sacred truths aligns with the doctrine of the Holy Ghost, through which Jesus Christ communicates with His followers, underscoring the continuity of divine revelation across generations.

name: Abinadom
desc: Nephite record-keeper; son of Chemish; slew many in battle

name: Joseph of Nazareth
desc: Husband of Mary; earthly guardian of Jesus
wikipedia_summary: According to the canonical Gospels, Joseph was a 1st-century Jewish man of Nazareth who was married to Mary, the mother of Jesus, and was the legal father of Jesus.

name: Anna
desc: Prophetess who recognized the infant Jesus in the temple

name: Isabel
desc: Harlot in the land of Siron who caused Corianton to forsake his mission
wikipedia_summary: Isabel is a female name of Spanish origin. It originates as the medieval Spanish form of Elisabeth. Arising in the 12th century, it became popular in England in the 13th century following the marriage of Isabella of Angoulême to the king of England. Variant forms and spellings include Isabella, Ysabelle, Isobel, and Isobelle.

name: John
desc: Beloved Apostle; translated; author of Revelation and the Gospel of John
wikipedia_summary: John the Apostle, also known as Saint John the Beloved and, in Eastern Orthodox Christianity, Saint John the Theologian, was one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus according to the New Testament. Generally listed as the youngest apostle, he was the son of Zebedee and Salome. His brother James was another of the Twelve Apostles. The Church Fathers identify him as John the Evangelist, John of Patmos, John the Elder, and the Beloved Disciple, and claim that he outlived the remaining apostles and was the only one to die of natural causes, although modern scholars are divided on the veracity of these

name: Mary Magdalene
desc: First witness of the resurrected Christ
wikipedia_summary: Mary Magdalene was a woman who, according to the four canonical gospels, travelled with Jesus as one of his followers and was a witness to his crucifixion and resurrection. In Gnostic writings, Mary Magdalene is depicted as Jesus's closest disciple who uniquely understood his teachings, causing tension with Peter, and is honoured as the "apostle to the apostles".

name: James the Less
desc: Apostle; son of Alphaeus; distinguished from James son of Zebedee
wikipedia_summary: James the Less is a figure of early Christianity. He is also called "the Minor", "the Little", "the Lesser", or "the Younger", according to translation; James is styled "the Less" to distinguish him from the Apostle James the Great, with "Less" meaning younger or shorter rather than less important.

name: Simon the Zealot
desc: Apostle; called the Zealot to distinguish him from Simon Peter
wikipedia_summary: Simon the Zealot, also the Canaanite or the Canaanean, was one of the apostles of Jesus. A few pseudepigraphical writings were connected to him, but Jerome does not include him in De viris illustribus written between 392 and 393 AD.

name: Moroni
desc: Son of Mormon; sealed the plates; last Nephite prophet; visited Joseph Smith

name: John the Revelator
desc: Translated Apostle; key figure in the Restoration of the priesthood
wikipedia_summary: John of Patmos is the name traditionally given to the author of the Book of Revelation. Revelation 1:9 states that John was on Patmos, an Aegean island off the coast of Roman Asia, where according to some biblical historians, he was exiled as a result of anti-Christian persecution under the Roman emperor Domitian.

name: Parley P. Pratt
desc: Apostle; missionary; author of Key to the Science of Theology and Voice of Warning
wikipedia_summary: Parley Parker Pratt Sr. was an early leader of the Latter Day Saint movement whose writings became a significant early nineteenth-century exposition of the Latter-Day Saint faith. Named in 1835 as one of the first members of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, Pratt was part of the Quorum's successful mission to Great Britain from 1839 to 1841. Pratt has been called "the Apostle Paul of Mormonism" for his promotion of distinctive Mormon doctrines.
christ_connection: [Matthew 2:1-2] Parley P. Pratt, as an Apostle of the Restoration, serves as a prophetic figure whose mission and teachings align with the covenantal promises of Christ. His writings, particularly [Key to the Science of Theology], reflect a deep theological engagement with the scriptures, illustrating the typological structure of the gospel. Through his role as a missionary and voice of warning, Pratt exemplifies the prophetic function of the apostles, whose ministry points forward to the ultimate revelation of Christ in the latter days. The covenantal relationship established through his writings underscores the enduring significance of Christ in the unfolding of sacred history.

name: Orson Pratt
desc: Apostle; mathematician; prolific pamphleteer on LDS doctrine
wikipedia_summary: Orson Pratt Sr. was an American religious leader and mathematician who was an original member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Christ. After the succession crisis Pratt continued in the Quorum of the Twelve of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and was a leading Mormon theologian and writer until his death.

name: John Taylor
desc: Third president of the Church; present at Carthage; 'the Lion of the Lord'

name: Wilford Woodruff
desc: Fourth president; ended polygamy by revelation; zealous record-keeper
wikipedia_summary: Wilford Woodruff Sr. was an American religious leader who served as the fourth president of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints from 1889 until his death. He ended the public practice of plural marriage among members of the LDS Church in 1890.

name: George Q. Cannon
desc: Counselor in the First Presidency; missionary to Hawaii; editor and publisher
wikipedia_summary: George Quayle Cannon was an early member of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, and served in the First Presidency under four successive presidents of the church: Brigham Young, John Taylor, Wilford Woodruff, and Lorenzo Snow. He was the church's chief political strategist, and was dubbed "the Mormon premier" and "the Mormon Richelieu" by the press. He was also a five-time Utah territorial delegate to the U.S. Congress.
